articles.title: Josh Turek says Kamala Harris should not campaign for him
articles.summary: Iowa Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek on Wednesday shot down the idea of former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigning for him. When pressed by a reporter at a Wednesday event in Cedar Rapids, Iowa about the topic of working with Harris during his campaign, Turek — a state representative and two-time Paralympic basketball gold medalist…
articles.body:
Iowa Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek on Wednesday shot down the idea of former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigning for him.

When pressed by a reporter at a Wednesday event in Cedar Rapids, Iowa about the topic of working with Harris during his campaign, Turek — a state representative and two-time Paralympic basketball gold medalist with a history of winning in conservative areas — simply responded, “No.”

Turek, who clinched his Senate nomination in early June, is the latest to join other red-state candidates who have attempted to distance themselves from the former vice president

His fellow Iowa Democrat, gubernatorial candidate Rob Sand, also pushed back against the idea of Harris campaigning for him — adding that he believes she shouldn’t pursue a presidential run in 2028.

“Let’s move on,” Sand said Wednesday. “We need some new leadership.”

Another red-state Democrat running for Senate, former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska), also recently separated herself from Harris.

The former vice president threw her support behind the Alaska Democrat in a fundraising email earlier this month, pressing supporters to send their funds to Peltola’s campaign. According to a New York Times report, however, Petola’s campaign claimed it did not request the endorsement from Harris and was not aware of the fundraising email before it was sent.

“Mary isn’t seeking endorsements from anyone from the Lower 48 — her focus is and always will be Alaska,” Peltola’s campaign said after Harris’s email.

Harris’s loss in the 2024 presidential race, along with Democrats’ failure to secure either chamber of Congress in that year’s elections, resulted in widespread platform division within the party. Democratic infighting about the party’s direction has lasted to this day, now primarily between progressive and establishment members.

But last month, former President Obama endorsed Turek. In a video from the Turek campaign , the Iowa candidate battled the former president in a game of “ IOWA” — a spin on the basketball game , “ HORSE.”

articles.summary: El ministro de Transportes responde a Michael O'Leary
articles.body: La discusión entre Ryanair y el ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, a través de la redes sociales sigue. El CEO de la aerolínea, Michael O'Leary, aseguró ayer que el político del PSOE debería aprender a sumar y restar. "La única solución es enviarle al ministro Puente esta semana el libro Matemáticas básicas para dummies, porque el ministro Puente es un dummy", indicó. El dirigente hasta le dedicó un vídeo para escenificar su respuesta. Óscar Puente no dudó en responder de nuevo a través de X, antes Twitter. "Sé sumar perfectamente. Las tasas de los aeropuertos españoles son lo suficientemente bajas para que una sola persona de Ryanair se haya embolsado 100 millones el año pasado", aseguró el titular de Transportes. Además, cerró su publicación con un mensaje contundente: "Ya sabes: si no te gustan nuestras reglas vuela a otro sitio". La discusión entre Ryanair y Óscar Puente viene de lejos y ha ido escalando con los últimos mensajes. La última polémica arrancó a raíz de una entrevista del ministro de Transportes en la que afirmó que la aerolínea pretendía rebajar las tasas aeroportuarias usando su falta de aviones para presionar. "Es una dinámica empresarial que disfraza sus problemas para introducir presión", declaró el político el pasado 23 de agosto. Desde entonces, la compañía ha replicado las observaciones de Óscar Puente constantemente, llegando al extremo de publicar un vídeo de su CEO, Michael O'Leary. No es la primera vez que la aerolínea exhibe una política de comunicación agresiva a través de sus redes sociales, con un tono que se aleja de la sobriedad y tratando temáticas que van más allá de lo puramente empresarial. El ministro de Transportes, por su parte, también es un político muy activo en las redes sociales y no ha dudado en entrar al trapo en este último conflicto con Ryanair.

articles.title: Man accused of using fake Chief Justice Roberts signature to get own criminal case dismissed
articles.summary: Joshua Culver allegedly forged Chief Justice John Roberts' signature on a fake Supreme Court dismissal order to get his Indiana criminal case thrown out.
articles.body: A man accused of using a forged signature of Chief Justice John Roberts on a bogus Supreme Court order in an alleged attempt to get his own Indiana criminal case dismissed has been arrested on federal charges, according to court documents. Joshua M. Culver, who authorities say also used the alias "Maverick A. Young," was arrested last Friday in Colorado after a federal grand jury in Indiana indicted him on four counts of falsely impersonating a U.S. officer or employee and one count involving the use of a forged federal judge's signature and court seal. Federal prosecutors allege Culver filed a document titled "Order of Dismissal With Prejudice" on Sept. 24, 2025, in a criminal case pending against him in Grant County Superior Court in Indiana. SUPREME COURT REJECTS MICHIGAN FAMILY'S CLAIM THAT COUNTY COMMITTED 'HOME EQUITY THEFT' OVER $2,200 TAX DEBT According to the indictment, the document used a forged signature of Roberts and a counterfeit U.S. Supreme Court seal in an effort to authenticate the purported dismissal order. The alleged scheme involving the nation's highest court was not Culver's first attempt to pass himself off as a federal official, prosecutors say. Five days before the alleged Roberts forgery, Culver allegedly posed as a National Security Agency agent while contacting the Tippecanoe County Sheriff's Office. According to the indictment, Culver used his purported authority as an NSA agent to make requests that prosecutors say the sheriff's office otherwise would not have fulfilled, including asking deputies to conduct a welfare check on his biological daughter and provide information about her location. MAN CLAIMING TO BE CARTEL MEMBER ALLEGEDLY THREATENS TO PUT 'GREEN LIGHT' ON COPS AND THEIR FAMILIES Culver also allegedly sought the names and information of sheriff's office employees and claimed he could take "adverse action" against the department in his purported capacity as an NSA agent. The following day, on Sept. 20, 2025, Culver allegedly called the workplace of an individual identified in the indictment only as "Individual A." Prosecutors say he falsely identified himself as a federal agent, claimed the person was "obstructing a federal investigation of a child kidnapping" and represented that he could have the individual arrested for committing a federal felony. He also allegedly asked the person's employer to intervene to obtain the individual's cooperation. JUSTICE NEIL GORSUCH BREAKS SILENCE ON VIOLENT THREATS AGAINST JUDICIARY, SUPREME COURT LEAKS Months later, in January 2026, Culver allegedly portrayed himself as a "Special Master enforcing orders of the United States Supreme Court" in a communication sent to the Lake County clerk and directed to a Superior Court judge. Prosecutors allege Culver claimed he had the authority to issue orders and warrants while demanding that the judge and court personnel take several actions, including making changes to vital records and dismissing cases and judgments against him. DOJ DEMANDS SANCTUARY STATES END 'BLATANTLY UNLAWFUL' ANTI-ICE POLICY AS A MATTER OF LIFE AND DEATH The indictment alleges Culver also warned that if officials failed to comply, he and U.S. Marshals would make arrests for "impeding a federal agent, lying to a federal agent, and conspiracy." Then, in February, Culver allegedly assumed yet another federal identity, this time portraying himself as the "Director of Tailored Access Operations," which the indictment describes as a purported intelligence agency. Prosecutors allege Culver filed a document titled "OFFICIAL SENSITIVE: TAILORED ACCESS OPERATIONS (TAO) COMPLIANCE DIRECTIVE" in Lake County Superior Court in a case pending against him. The document, which purported to bear official letterhead, allegedly described Culver as a "federal asset" involved in multiple investigations and demanded that officials take a series of actions under a purported "federal directive." Those demands included dismissing the case against Culver with prejudice, quashing warrants and requiring Lake County officials to cooperate with a purported "federal audit," according to the indictment. articles.title: MORNING GLORY: Hasan Piker’s radical rhetoric is becoming Democrats’ 2026 brand
articles.summary: Unlike Marx or Lenin, far-left streamer Hasan Piker shows no evidence of serious study, yet his radical Twitch presence now defines the Democratic Party brand in 2026.
articles.body: At least Marx, Lenin and Mao were well read. Social media influencer Hasan Piker wears his Mao jacket and hoses his Twitch audience down with absurd political takes that do not betray any evidence that Rutgers University obliged him to read even a book or two of serious history before he graduated in 2013. Rutgers is a fine school and anyone can get a great education there, but Piker’s "body of work" shows us that serious study there is quite obviously not obligatory. In the course of doing so, he has become the face of the Democratic Party in the 2026 midterms, and has personally carried the most radical major-party candidate in memory — Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed — to his party’s nomination for United States Senate. Elissa Slotkin — and others, like New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker, have slapped Piker down by name. Piker learned the ropes of the "attention economy" there, then amplified the schtick right on through the land of the "outrage economy" and into what Mary Katharine Ham of the "Getting Hammered" podcast described to her co-host Vic Matus last week as the "personality disorder attention economy." ELISSA SLOTKIN CALLS OUT HASAN PIKER FOR BLAMING JEWISH AMERICANS TARGETED OVER THEIR ISRAEL VIEWS That approach to garnering audience and thus profits was on display this weekend with Piker’s revolting mocking of grief around Kirk’s murder, a video that will injure every Democrat associated with him, most especially Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrats’ candidate for Senate in Michigan, whom Piker got over the top for the nomination with a closing campaign blitz (and pool party). The DSA-adjacent hard-left Senate candidates among the Democrats — like Troy Jackson in Maine, James Talarico in Texas, and Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota — are also getting pulled down by Piker. Piker may never have met or even spoken with or about these candidates, but he has become the new face of the Democratic Party, its new "voice." Piker, like the DSA, is now effectively running with every Democrat in every race. JONATHAN TURLEY: PIKER'S CHARLIE KIRK ATTACK SHOWS HE IS HATEFUL LEFT'S PIED PIPER The DSA is said to have about 120,000 dues-paying members. It appears to have nearly as many co-chairs, and not one of them can make a coherent argument about anything but their "we hate the Constitution" takes, while their extreme rhetoric has laid an oily film over every Democratic candidate. It’s how you build a majority." SCHUMER DODGES QUESTION ON WHETHER DSA BELONGS IN DEMOCRATIC PARTY That’s a lot of copium. Senate Majority Leader John Thune doesn’t have to play that game. articles.title: Gender equity, DEI, climate action: How the Smithsonian’s woke push ‘infiltrated’ America's most beloved Zoo
articles.summary: The Smithsonian National Zoo embraced DEI initiatives, LGBTQ programming, and climate change messaging that critics say strays from its mission.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: As the Trump administration continues to crack down on far-left messaging and agenda items within the Smithsonian Institution, a Fox News Digital review found that the Smithsonian National Zoo has been adopting "woke" messaging and programming of its own over the past several years. Smithsonian's National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute, which hosts roughly 2 million visitors each year at its Washington, D.C. national zoo and operates a global conservation research program spanning more than 40 countries, has placed an emphasis on issues like DEI and climate change, according to its own website. "Gender equity, civil liberties and justice are necessary ingredients for peace and prosperity, but they also have a direct impact on resource use and climate change," a 2021 article on the organization’s website reads. The article, written by seabird ecologist Autumn-Lynn Harrison and coral biologist Mary Hagedorn, makes the case that "one direct way we can bolster climate action is by addressing inequities in health and education across the globe." TRUMP V. SMITHSONIAN: A TIMELINE OF HOW THE WHITE HOUSE FIGHT OVER 'WOKE' HISTORY UNFOLDED Searching "climate change" on the Zoo’s website yields almost 400 results, including articles warning about its impacts on vernal pools, salamanders, wildfires, coral nurseries, and a variety of other aspects of wildlife. In addition to attempting to root out political messaging in the Smithsonian, which Fox News Digital has extensively reported on, the Trump administration has also placed a focus on rooting out DEI practices within the federal government, practices that appear to be a high priority for the Smithsonian Zoo. "Diversity and inclusion are integral to all aspects of the Smithsonian Institution's operations and key components of the Smithsonian Strategic Plan," the 2023 Smithsonian Diversity and Inclusion Initiatives Report, which includes several pages specific to the Zoo’s DEI efforts, explains. SMITHSONIAN EXEC WHO SAID DEI 'MUST BE AT THE CENTER' OF INSTITUTIONS IS RAKING IN EYE-POPPING SALARY The report outlines several DEI programs undertaken by the National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute during that fiscal year, including diversity-focused internships, LGBTQ family programming at the Zoo featuring rainbow-themed animal enrichment, and efforts to promote inclusive language in the Zoo and aquarium profession. "Americans visit zoos to learn about conservation efforts and admire animals, not to be shamed or feel guilt-ridden," Independent Women’s Forum Center for Energy and Conservation director Gabriella Hoffman told Fox News Digital. "Conservation has, sadly, been infiltrated by elements of DEI, ESG, and climate alarmism. This invites confusion and division into a space that should be science-first." A 2021 Smithsonian Magazine article promoted how the National Zoo helped launch the Association of Minority Zoo and Aquarium Professionals, aimed at increasing racial and ethnic minority representation in Zoo and aquarium careers through networking, outreach, mentorship and professional development. "As the curator of large carnivores at the Smithsonian’s National Zoo and a black man in the zoo field, I have long been keenly aware of the dearth of black and brown faces in my chosen field," Smithsonian curator Craig Saffoe wrote in the article headlined: "Why a Group of Zoo and Aquarium Professionals Wants to Ensure the Future of Their Field Is More Inclusive." "After years of thinking about what I could do to try to address this situation, I finally decided to, as my mother told me growing up, ‘stop talking about it, and be about it.’" FORMER DEMOCRATIC STAFFERS, DEI LEADERS SHAPE SMITHSONIAN LEADERSHIP AMID POLITICAL FIRESTORM LGBTQ family programming has been a consistent theme at the Smithsonian’s National Zoo which has used its annual International Family Equality Day to conduct outreach to the LGBTQ community. The free event, which the Zoo says it has hosted annually since 2018, has featured animal encounters, keeper talks, music, games and community activities. Zoo staff have also created rainbow-themed animal enrichment and treats, including colorful ice cakes, for animals throughout the park. The event expanded its community partnerships in 2024, when the Zoo hosted representatives from the DC Center for the LGBTQ Community, SMYAL, Rainbow Families, Brave Trails and the Smithsonian Pride Alliance. The program included a performance by the LGBTQ-and-allied GenOUT Youth Chorus, a community picnic with local LGBTQ organizations and music that highlighted queer identity and inclusion. The outside groups referred to the gathering as "Gay Day at the Zoo," while the Zoo’s programming was formally billed as International Family Equality Day. "In places like the National Zoo, especially a taxpayer-funded organization like the National Zoo, zoos have a primary mission of conservation and species management, habitat management, that kind of thing, and when ideologies, or at least science that is in question, start to take over and really rule the management of an organization like the zoo, then you start to have problems," Jason Hayes, a Senior Research Fellow with the Heritage Foundation's Center for Energy, Climate, and Environment, told Fox News Digital. In January 2025, the Smithsonian organization announced that it was eliminating its Office of Diversity in line with the Trump administration’s efforts but noted it is "retaining our efforts at visitor accessibility as it serves a critical function." However, several work profiles listed on the Zoo’s website as of this week still contain language suggesting DEI is part of their daily activities, including the Zoo’s profile of Elliott Ferguson, president and CEO of Destination DC and a member of the Zoo’s advisory board, which says advancing the tourism and hospitality industry is a priority for him and that his work includes "diversity, equity and inclusion," conversations about racism and expanding opportunities for people of color." The profile also notes that he previously chaired Tourism Diversity Matters, a hospitality-workforce organization focused on DEI. SMITHSONIAN'S TAXPAYER FUNDS FACE CHOPPING BLOCK AS GOP DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY FOR 'WOKE' HISTORY Ricardo Stanoss, the Smithsonian’s National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute’s director for conservation capacity, was listed in the FY2023 diversity report as the principal investigator for an in-progress community advisory group that held listening sessions with D.C. leaders and explored development of a diversity-focused internship program and a master’s degree focused on environmental justice and climate change. Additionally, The Zoo’s Great Plains Science Program website currently lists "Inclusion" among its core values, pledging to create pathways for people from underrepresented groups to participate in its work and cultivate a new generation of conservationists. Several of the researchers associated with that project have biographies that underscore its emphasis on inclusion and Native community engagement. The Zoo also continues to partner with groups that have made DEI a central focus, including the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA), of which the Zoo is a long-standing accredited member. The Zoo participates in AZA conservation and animal-management programs and must meet its accreditation standards, including a requirement that member institutions maintain written plans for accessible, welcoming organizational cultures. AZA’s website says DEI is "embedded in everything we do" and the group wrote in 2020 that "systemic racism is embedded in our structures, culture and organizations, and we are committed to positive and sustained change that dismantles these barriers." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Brandie Smith, the current director of the Smithsonian’s National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute, joined the Smithsonian in 2008 after spending 10 years as AZA’s vice president of animal conservation. Beyond its AZA accreditation, the Smithsonian is a member of the International Union for Conservation of Nature, a global conservation organization whose current gender policy calls for gender-responsive conservation and inclusive participation across race, sexual orientation and gender identity. The policy governs IUCN staff and is advisory for member institutions. The Zoo also works with the Zoological Society of London on the scimitar-horned oryx recovery effort. ZSL’s FAIRER Conservation program says it uses a "decolonial lens" and aims to embed "justice, equity and inclusion" in its conservation work. Fox News Digital asked the Smithsonian’s National Zoo for comment and inquired about any current implementation of DEI in the organization but did not receive a response. Instead, a spokesperson provided a statement saying, "The Smithsonian’s National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute is the Nation’s Zoo—a place where people can experience wildlife, learn about the natural world and see conservation in action." The spokesperson added, "The Zoo connects millions of people with wildlife while advancing a global mission to save species." Hoffman explained that "activists have long targeted zoos simply because they exist." "Kowtowing to these extremists — thinking the crocodile will eat you last by adopting these views — will invite extinction, not longevity," Hoffman said. "The Smithsonian Zoo shouldn't alienate visitors with political lectures and empty platitudes. The zoo should stick to showcasing pandas, not pandering to radicals. More imperiled species would be conserved and recovered today by de-emphasizing woke policies that are anathema to conservation efforts."

articles.title: Spanberger AG draws fire over two-front fight against Trump enforcement agenda
articles.summary: Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones faces fire over a civil rights probe into Greene County Sheriff Steve Smith's ICE-involved traffic stop operations.
articles.body: Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones is drawing fire over two disputes involving the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement agenda — a civil rights investigation into a rural sheriff’s traffic-stop practices amid his cooperation with ICE. and a legal challenge involving federal access to commercial driver records. Virginia House Minority Leader Terry Kilgore told Fox News Digital that the two disputes reflect what he characterized as a broader unwillingness by Virginia’s Democratic leadership to cooperate with President Donald Trump. His criticism came as Jones announced a probe into Greene County Sheriff Steve Smith. "That's just this whole administration's modus operandi, to put it bluntly, they are so mad at Trump, they want to make sure they don't want to cooperate with Trump in any area whatsoever, and they want make it unsafe for Virginians," Kilgore, R-Gate City, told Fox News Digital in an interview. FIRST ON FOX: DOJ SUES SPANBERGER’S VIRGINIA OVER LAWS KNEECAPPING FEDERAL AGENTS AS MASK WAR ESCALATES The criticism comes as Jones’ Office of Civil Rights notified Smith that it launched an investigation into allegations involving the Greene County Sheriff’s Office’s traffic-stop practices and cooperation with federal immigration authorities. "I applaud the Greene County sheriff for working with ICE to make that we don't have illegals on our roads, illegals out here committing crimes and things of that nature, unlike our attorney general, who's the chief law enforcement officer of our state out here picking fights with sheriffs over illegal immigrants," Kilgore said. The dispute comes amid a broader shift in Virginia’s immigration enforcement policy under Spanberger On her first day in office, Spanberger — who endorsed Jones — rescinded former Gov. Glenn Youngkin’s order encouraging ICE cooperation. She later signed a law on April 22 sponsored by Del. Alfonso Lopez, D-Arlington, restricting state and local participation in federal civil immigration enforcement. ICE RESUMES NATIONWIDE TRAFFIC STOPS UNDER NEW POLICY REQUIRING BODY CAMERAS "[My office] has reviewed allegations that GCSO may be conducting traffic stops in violation of state law and the Constitution," Jones’ Office of Civil Rights wrote to Smith while demanding records concerning immigration enforcement policies, training materials and interagency agreements. Smith’s deputies have participated in several operations with ICE — notable for a small, rural county located along major transportation routes. A June operation near the intersection of U.S. 29 and U.S. 33 resulted in 49 people being detained by ICE. U.S. 29 connects Washington, D.C., with Charlottesville and points south, while U.S. 33 connects Richmond with western Virginia. A Honduran man identified by DHS as an MS-13 gang member was among 26 people arrested during another operation in nearby Ruckersville in May. "Tell me what kind of message that's sending to the citizens of Virginia — that it's more important for me to protect illegal folks who are here illegally than to protect our citizens here," Kilgore said. Smith had previously defended his operations in comments to Charlottesville media, saying his deputies apply reasonable suspicion — "the same as we do for all vehicles" — as the standard for initiating traffic stops. Local activists accused deputies of profiling, while Smith said speeding, failure to maintain a lane and running red lights most often prompt traffic stops. "Oh, look, the Virginia AG is going after a cop for doing actual cop things," former Del. Nick Freitas added in a statement. Fox News Digital reached out to Jones, Spanberger and ICE for comment. Smith declined to comment to Fox News Digital, citing his retention of counsel, but previously told the Piedmont Journal-Recorder that he will "continue to assist ICE with their operations" after discussing the new law with Del. Karen Hamilton, R-Stanardsville. State Sen. Creigh Deeds, D-Charlottesville, the Democrats’ 2009 gubernatorial nominee whose district neighbors Greene County, said he was "disappointed" by the situation. "Certainly we all want people who come into this country to come in legally, but the people that are here are for the most part here to fill a need and that’s work," he told CVilleRightNow. Former Del. Kim Taylor, R-Petersburg, who received a politically motivated death threat during the 2025 election, referenced graphic text messages Jones sent to another former lawmaker imagining the murder of former Virginia House Speaker Todd Gilbert, R-Shenandoah. The "two bullets" scandal nearly torpedoed Jones’ campaign. TRUMP ADMIN TRUCKING CRACKDOWN LANDS 51 IMMIGRATION DETENTIONS, 36 ENGLISH LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY VIOLATIONS Taylor told Fox News Digital that she considers Jones’ actions hypocritical given his past messages. "For an attorney general who once talked about putting ‘two bullets’ in a political opponent to now lecture law enforcement is hypocrisy at its worst," she said. Alongside his investigation into Smith, Jones joined a lawsuit challenging the Trump administration’s demand for a bulk transfer of commercial-driver records covering roughly 17 million drivers as the U.S. Department of Transportation cracks down on drivers who cannot meet English-language requirements or illegal immigrant truckers accused of causing deadly wrecks. Jones celebrated U.S. District Judge Anthony Trenga, a George W. Bush appointee, temporarily blocking the bulk transfer of the records, calling it an "important win for protecting the privacy of millions of commercial drivers." An ICE spokesperson confirmed the Ruckersville operation near US-29, including the arrests of 49 illegal immigrants."All of the illegal aliens were transported to ICE facilities for further processing and will receive due process. They will remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings," the spokesperson said. "Partnerships with law enforcement are critical to having the resources we need to arrest illegal aliens across the country. When politicians bar local law enforcement from working with DHS, our law enforcement officers have to have a more visible presence so that we can find and apprehend the criminals let out of jails and back into communities," they added. Kilgore, whose southwestern Virginia district includes mountainous stretches of U.S. 58 and lies near Interstate 81, told Fox News Digital that the suit is "just another way that they try to stick their thumb in the administration's eye." SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER "Once again, we're siding with illegals or foreigners who are here driving 18-wheelers… who could harm our citizens because they're not qualified," Kilgore said. articles.title: Lutnick floats new way to add Trump’s name to Kennedy Center
articles.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick suggested a new way Thursday for President Trump’s name to reappear on the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. Lutnick told reporters outside of a Thursday hearing that the center could “acknowledge President Trump” for his role in proposed renovations. The Trump administration earlier this week said in a…
articles.body:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick suggested a new way Thursday for President Trump’s name to reappear on the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.

Lutnick told reporters outside of a Thursday hearing that the center could “acknowledge President Trump” for his role in proposed renovations. The Trump administration earlier this week said in a court filing that without its recommended construction, the renowned center may need to be demolished .

“Underneath the name of the building, which will remain the John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts, Renovated and Restored by President Donald J. Trump,” Lutnick said.

The full name — pending a federal judge’s approval — is meant to recognize the work the Trump administration would do to fix what Lutnick called “decades of financial regret.”

“The building is dangerous. People say, ‘oh, don’t overstate that it’s dangerous. Look, there are chunks of concrete falling off the ceiling in the garage,’” he said.

Lutnick continued, Trump’s “doing it for the American people. Because if it takes years to renovate this building and it will take two years to renovate it, he’s not doing it for himself.”

The Commerce secretary also said renovations are expected to cost $257 million.

He clarified that the proposed renovations would keep the REACH — a new addition to the Kennedy Center campus — walking back previous controversial proposals that included its full closure.

On Monday, Department of Justice (DOJ) lawyers similarly argued that Trump’s name not appearing on the center would cause “donors to flee, financial contributions to dry up and structural rehabilitation to stop.”

“There will simply not be the expertise or funding necessary to rebuild and renovate this decimated structure,” they continued.

Lutnick echoed the DOJ’s claims Thursday, saying only Trump would be able to raise $500 million for renovations — unlike the center’s other board members.

Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-Ohio), an ex officio member of the Kennedy Center board, has continually opposed Trump’s attempts to add his name to the center. She’s specifically accused the board, which Trump chairs, of trying to get around an earlier ruling from U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper barring the previous name addition.

“Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it,” Cooper wrote in his June ruling.

articles.title: GOP governor says he asked attorney general to look into ‘aggressive’ DOJ election observers
articles.summary: Wyoming Gov. Mark Gordon (R) on Wednesday said election monitors deployed to the state by the Department of Justice (DOJ) were behaving in an “aggressive” and “irregular” manner during the primary election. “It sounded like the behavior of the observers was a bit aggressive,” he said at a state canvassing board meeting Wednesday, according to…
articles.body:
Wyoming Gov. Mark Gordon (R) on Wednesday said election monitors deployed to the state by the Department of Justice (DOJ) were behaving in an “aggressive” and “irregular” manner during the primary election.

“It sounded like the behavior of the observers was a bit aggressive,” he said at a state canvassing board meeting Wednesday, according to NBC News .

He later added that their “behavior seemed to exceed what the authority that Congress had given them was.”

Last Tuesday, Wyoming Secretary of State Chuck Gray earned the GOP party nomination for the House, while former state Sen. Lisa Kinney won the Democratic primary for the Cowboy State’s at-large seat in the lower chamber.

While voters cast their ballots, Debra Lee, a Laramie County clerk, said poll monitors began to ask questions about their tabulators and training guides for poll workers.

Lee told NBC News she refused to allow those deployed from the DOJ to interview voters and noted that some of their questions were “outside the scope of federal voting rights laws.”

“Shortly after learning of their presence, I spoke with a DOJ official in Washington who informed me that the decision to deploy monitors to Wyoming was made on short notice, and an email had been sent to me, but it may have gone to the wrong address,” Lee continued.

For years, the DOJ has deployed election monitors to states to observe voting across the country.

Last week, the DOJ said 1,000 poll monitors would be deployed during the midterms; dozens had already been deployed to observe primaries including the Tuesday runoff for the GOP Senate nomination in South Carolina.

“Voters deserve absolute confidence that their ballots are secure and their voices are heard without interference,” Darin Smith, the U.S. attorney for the District of Wyoming, said in a statement last week regarding poll monitors in the state.

“We are working alongside local officials to ensure every lawful vote is protected,” he added.

The minutes from Wednesday’s state canvassing meeting say Smith was informed of Gordon’s concerns regarding poll monitors’ behavior during voting.

articles.title: El-Sayed says he has ‘no plans’ to campaign with Piker
articles.summary: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed says he has “no plans” to campaign with left-wing streamer Hasan Piker after a slew of Democratic lawmakers criticized Piker for his remarks on American Jews supporting Israel. During an interview with Semafor in the Detroit suburbs, El-Sayed denied that Piker will play a role in his race against…
articles.body:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed says he has “no plans” to campaign with left-wing streamer Hasan Piker after a slew of Democratic lawmakers criticized Piker for his remarks on American Jews supporting Israel.

During an interview with Semafor in the Detroit suburbs, El-Sayed denied that Piker will play a role in his race against former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.), in the fight to succeed outgoing Sen. Gary Peters (D-Mich.).

“Most people are a lot more worried about things like, what are you going to do about my groceries? What are you going to do about my healthcare? What are you going to do about the fact that I cannot afford [to enroll] my kid in baseball, even though my kid’s a really great baseball player?” El-Sayed told the outlet.

“Those are the things I’m talking about, and the effort to make this race about a streamer in LA [Los Angeles] is actually kind of laughable,” he added, referring to Piker.

Piker, a left-wing commentator with 1.7 million followers on the social platform X, recently said that while Jewish Americans do not automatically support the Israeli government, “Jewish institutions” are “teaching people the idea that Jews are monolithic.”

He said on a livestream, “If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews,” while displaying a photo of Michigan state Sen. Jeremy Moss (D) and his contributions from “pro-Israel” donors.

Moss, who is Jewish and broadly supports Israel, is running to succeed Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.), whom El-Sayed defeated in the Democratic Senate primary earlier this month.

Forty percent of religious Jews feel very or extremely emotionally attached to Israel, while 11 percent of secular Jews felt that way, based on a poll The Associated Press-NORC conducted in June.

Piker’s remarks drew backlash from a lengthy list of Democratic officials, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (N.Y.).

“The malicious claim that American Jews are inviting violence against themselves is dangerous and antisemitic,” Jeffries wrote Monday on X . “There is zero justification for threats against the safety of our Jewish brothers and sisters at a moment of rising hate.

“We will fight the cancer of antisemitism with the fierce urgency of now.”

El-Sayed also publicly disagreed with Piker’s comments, saying in a Monday statement he believes “all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence.

The progressive candidate added, “This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past. My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters. Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk.”

During the Democratic primary, Piker joined El-Sayed on the campaign trail — continuing his trend of backing left-wing candidates across the country. The streamer has blasted the Israeli government’s military campaign in Gaza, calling it a “genocide.”
